segments.he: הרב הצדיק מבארדיטשוב ז"ל אמר שכשמגיע ימים נוראים דוקר לו בגבו "אז ער גאט ימים נוראים שטעחט אים דיא פליידע" ואמר מהרנ"ת ז"ל ע"ז מי שאין דוקר לו כמה צריך שידקור לו בגבו "דער וואס שטעכט אים ניט וויפול בארץ מים שוין שטעדין:
segments.en:
Reb Shmuel the Alef grew up from his youth with the Seer of Lublin. His father Reb Avraham Peretz was among the disciples of the Seer of Lublin and was the Seer's ba'al toke'ah. And the Seer loved Reb Shmuel greatly and commanded his father to travel with him to Eretz Yisroel — and there he would perform wonders. And so from his youth his father traveled with him to Tzfas, where he afterward became the Chief Rabbi and Mara d'Asra. He was wise in all branches of wisdom — including the wisdom of medicine, in which he was greatly renowned. He was practically the physician for all those regions — and gentiles too would come to him by the hundreds and thousands from all their places to be healed. Many times he would travel to their villages or towns and stay with them several days and nights for their healing. And whatever they wanted to pay him as a fee he refused to accept — only telling them to instruct their children after them to be lovers of Israel, and that if they should see a Jew straying to bring him home. And so he always planted love of Israel in their hearts — and so it was until those days that they loved Israel more than in other towns of Eretz Yisroel — and in particular the grandchildren of Reb Shmuel they honored greatly, calling them "children of the Sage Shmuel" and saying they recognized them by their faces. And they told me that even on Rosh HaShanah he was in the house of study — and rows of Arabs and Arab women would stand outside in the streets, having come to be healed. He would go out before the shofar blowing — and at that time his mind was not at all free, as is well known for him before the shofar blowing. Nonetheless he would tell each one whatever came to his mouth for their healing — and so it was done until he had finished with them all. And after Yom Tov they all came with gifts and thanks. And all of this he did for love of Israel.

And he edited and helped print Reb Yisroel of Shklov's book Pe'as HaShulchan — and they made a great feast, at which Reb Yisroel was fasting a series of three days. He did not want to break his fast — and also did not want it known that he was fasting. Therefore he was compelled to eat at the feast, where everyone saw him — and in truth ate nothing from the feast, only managing cleverly so that everyone thought he was eating while in reality he was not at all. Reb Shmuel the Alef had the custom to bless all his grandchildren on Erev Yom Kippur. His sons would bring all his grandchildren to him. All of them he blessed — only one granddaughter he did not bless. They brought her to him again and he turned his face away and would not bless her. They brought her once more — and again he would not bless her. A few days afterward that granddaughter passed away, G-d preserve us. And they understood after the fact that he had known beforehand that a death sentence had been decreed upon her — and therefore he had not blessed her.
